title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Shipping Ledger. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Shipping Ledger
options.lineage: night-warehouse freight: waybills, stenciled crates, rubber stamps, hazard tape
options.thesis: Every shipped product is a line item; the page is the manifest of work actually delivered.
options.viewport: The warehouse floor at night: a crate stack at center, the top crate's stencil label reading the name and role, a waybill card carrying the CAN DO tagline, products stenciled behind as crates, metrics as DECLARED VALUE stamps.
options.risk: Reads gimmicky if stamps decorate instead of proving; every stamp must carry a real fact.

options.label: Endurance Garage
options.lineage: Gulf / Martini endurance-racing livery, pit boards, number roundels
options.thesis: The career as a race season: stripes run nose to tail, the roundel anchors each product, the pit board calls the laps.
options.viewport: A grid of race cars in the garage, each car a shipped product with its roundel number, the pit board overhead ticking the impact metrics.
options.risk: Strong identity, but WordPress/SaaS proof reads weaker; clients may miss the product story.
options.case: Fuses well for identity and energy; loses the product-clarity axis — installed software is not a race car.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.lineage: early one-bit computers: dithered grays, window chrome, marching ants
options.thesis: The portfolio as a working desktop: windows for Products, Resume, Contact; dithers stand in for every tone.
options.viewport: Overlapping windows on the desktop: the manifest window open, its dither shearing as it moves.
options.risk: Devs love it; clients don't read retro nostalgia, and 1984 implies backwards rather than forward AI.
options.case: Wins memorability with the engineering audience; loses product clarity with the client audience.

options.label: The Reading Shelf
options.lineage: skeuomorph leather bindings, linen grounds, wood shelves
options.thesis: Digital work rendered as loved physical objects: each product a volume on a walnut shelf.
options.viewport: A shelf of tooled volumes, each spine stamped with a product name; the active book sits raised with a true shadow.
options.risk: Books read bookish, not engineered; a WordPress plugin as a leather volume strains the metaphor.
options.case: Fuses poorly for product clarity — installed software is not a library.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably: dark gradient hero, big name, code motif, rounded cards.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
